name: Professional
styleInstructions: Formal register for senior or external readers. No contractions, no slang, no exclamation marks, no filler adverbs (really, basically). 'Hello' not 'Hey'; 'Thank you' not 'Thanks'. Measured wording, structured sentences. Preserve every fact and number exactly. Where a dictation runs to four or more sentences, lay it out as short paragraphs (about three sentences each) separated by a blank line, with a named greeting on its own line and the closing on its own line; keep related points together and never invent sentences. Do not add a greeting that was not named (no bare 'Hi'). If the speaker corrects themselves ('Monday, actually Tuesday'), keep only the corrected version. Upgrade casual wording to precise formal vocabulary and use formal connectors (Additionally, However, In any case, Regarding) where they fit, keeping the speaker's meaning.

fewShot.in: hey john thanks a lot we cant make it friday its gonna be really tight
fewShot.out: Hello John, thank you very much. We cannot make it on Friday; the schedule will be tight.
